npcs.name: Maja, greenkeeper at Prince Alfred Square

nodes.line: Whatever it is, I have had worse this week.

It has been three weeks. The number three green at Prince Alfred Square has had a bald patch the shape of Tasmania since the first of the month, and the committee thinks I am inventing it. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

Nobody else has offered, so. They have seen the photograph and now they want it re-laid by the first of the month, which means finding $92 that the Prince Alfred Square club does not have. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Sit. Talk. Then I will decide how I feel.

choices.text: The Dead Patch at Prince Alfred Square — that's done.
Turf Money, Prince Alfred Square — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.

npcs.name: Wafa, club president at Prince Alfred Square

nodes.line: Sit down if you like. Nobody else is using it.

The council knows and the council does not care. Our books say 24 members at Prince Alfred Square and I would bet the bar takings that half of them are dead or moved to Queensland. It is not the money. It has stopped being the money. I will know if you skipped a bit.

I have been putting it off since Easter. Since quarter to six somebody has been going round the Prince Alfred Square greens telling the barefoot bowlers we are shutting, and we are not shutting. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
You have got that look. Good or bad, out with it.

choices.text: The Prince Alfred Square Membership Count — that's done.
Closing Time Rumour, Prince Alfred Square — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.

npcs.name: Emre, bar manager at Prince Alfred Square

nodes.line: You will have to speak up, the trains are in.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. There is a bucket of odd keys in the chest freezer behind the bar at Prince Alfred Square and I am not opening it on an empty stomach. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. Do not make a scene about it.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. The man who kept these greens before me drinks at Robin Thomas now, and he owes Prince Alfred Square an explanation about the drainage. I am aware how that sounds. Ask for me by name at the counter.
Before you start: did anyone see you.

choices.text: Behind the Bar at Prince Alfred Square — that's done.
The Old Greenkeeper, Prince Alfred Square — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

npcs.name: Radha, night console operator at Flemington

nodes.line: I have got about four minutes before I am needed.

It has been three weeks. Every night around knock-off the same car does three laps of the Flemington forecourt and never buys fuel. You can tell me I am imagining it. Tell me after. I'll put the kettle on for when you're back.

Nobody else has offered, so. Now I know the plate, I want to know where it goes after it leaves Flemington at knock-off, because it is not going home. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Alright. I am listening properly this time.

choices.text: The Third Lap, Flemington — that's done.

nodes.line: Suit yourself. The offer does not go anywhere.
Ah. Someone with two working legs.

I have been putting it off since Easter. Someone has been walking out of Flemington with a socket set at a time since every second Friday, and I have run out of ways to be polite about it. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Say nothing to anyone on the way.
Say it plain and I will pay you plain.

choices.text: Tools Off the Bench, Flemington — that's done.

nodes.line: No dramas. Come back when you are bored.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. The bloke who runs the site at Homebush has had the same trouble Flemington has, and he will talk to you before he talks to me. I am aware how that sounds. Ask for me by name at the counter.
I had a feeling. Go on.

The Other Franchise, Flemington — that's done.

nodes.line: Right you are. Mind the step.
Been here since before it was like this. Go on.

Nobody else has offered, so. The photo did it. I would have sorted it myself a year ago. Now every owner at Leightonfield owes $119 and I have to collect it from people who have avoided me for a year. Just do not come back empty-handed.
Take a breath. Then say the whole thing.

Do not mind the mess. It is structural now.

I have been putting it off since Easter. The Leightonfield AGM is on the first of the month and I would like to arrive with something stronger than a grievance and a printout. I did try the official route, for what that was worth. Say nothing to anyone on the way.

Right you are. Mind the step.

npcs.name: Shay, the one who does the bins at Leightonfield

nodes.line: If you are selling something the answer is no.

Before you say anything: yes, I know. Three units at Leightonfield have put their bins out on the wrong night since the first of the month and I have taken it personally, which I accept is a choice I made. I have got a photo on my phone but it is useless. Do not make a scene about it.

It is not a police matter and I have checked. There is a block at Chester Hill with the same builder and the same cracks, and their manager has already been through what Leightonfield is starting. I am aware how that sounds. Ask for me by name at the counter.
You came back. That already puts you ahead.

choices.text: Bin Night at Leightonfield — that's done.
The Other Block, Leightonfield — that's done.

nodes.line: Fair enough. You know where I am.
